Hello HeliumDeploy Support,
My Hammer BC04 and NerdQaxe++ Rev7 both stopped mining on the HarloLabs pool at around 10 p.m. last night (Mountain Time). They had been connected and mining earlier that evening.
I pointed them to another pool, and both connected successfully. I also ran tracert pool.harlolabs.com from my PC. The hostname resolved and the trace completed in seven hops, but I haven’t tested whether the Stratum port is accepting connections.
Could you check whether the HarloLabs pool had an outage or configuration change around that time? Please confirm the current pool address, port, and required worker/login format for these miners.
Miners: Hammer BC04 and NerdQaxe++ Rev7
Pool address I was using: pool.harlolabs.com (port 8888)

Thank you,
Dean
Note to the team: I'll check our notes on the HarloLabs pool before answering.
Searched the web · pool.harlolabs.com stratum
Handed to the team · I have no pool status or server logs, so I cannot confirm an outage or config ch

Hi Dean,

Your testing already narrows this down a lot. Both miners dropped at the same moment and both connect fine to another pool, so the hardware is almost certainly fine. The problem is between your network and the Harlo Pool stratum port, or on the pool side.

I can't see the pool's server status or logs, so I can't tell you for sure whether there was an outage or a config change around 10 p.m. Mountain Time. I've passed that question to JD, our hardware lead, along with everything you've tested. The team is offline for the weekend. They'll pick it up Monday at 10am ET and reply in this thread.

Here are the settings currently published on our Harlo Pool page.
The stratum URL is stratum+tcp://pool.harlolabs.com:8888, the worker is your BCH address, and the password is x.
 So pool.harlolabs.com on port 8888 is still the published address. If your worker field has anything other than a plain Bitcoin Cash address in it, that's worth checking, but since both miners were mining fine earlier that evening, I doubt it's the cause.

Tracert only tests ICMP, so it proves the host is reachable but not that the stratum port is open. To check the port from your PC, open PowerShell and run: Test-NetConnection pool.harlolabs.com -Port 8888

If it says TcpTestSucceeded : True, the port is accepting connections from your network. In that case, the most useful thing is the miner's own log line when it tries to connect. On the NerdQaxe++ that's the Logs page in its web UI. The BC04 shows its connection status on its own status or log page. Look for whatever comes right after it tries to connect: a refused connection, a timeout or an authorization error. If it says False, the port isn't reachable from your network right now, which points to the pool being down or something blocking port 8888.

If you'd like a faster answer than Monday, JD and the community are very active on the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Mention @nullhashrate with what you've found, and it's also the quickest place to see if other miners lost the pool at the same time.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Regards,

FYI. Still no connect

Hi Dean,

Thanks for the screenshot. I think it shows the problem.

Your PowerShell test reached us-east.harlolabs.com on port 8888 and shows TcpTestSucceeded : True. So your network can reach the pool's mining server.

On the Nerd Rev7, though, Pool 1 is set to us-east.pool.harlolabs.com and shows as Offline. That has an extra "pool." in the middle. It's a different name from the one your PC just reached, so the miner is trying a server that isn't there.

To fix it, open Pool 1 on the Nerd Rev7 and change the host to exactly us-east.harlolabs.com. Leave the port at 8888, keep your BCH address as the worker and x as the password, then save. If the BC04 has the same host, change it there too.

Everything else on the Nerd looks healthy. It's mining at 5.0 TH/s on your other three pools with almost no rejects, and the temperatures are well inside their limits.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Subject: Pool changes caused my miners to disconnect
I got both my Hammer and NerdQaxe 7 connected again, but only after figuring out that the pool setup had changed.
My old account was gone, so I created a new one. The current setup is very different: the server address and worker format have changed, and the payout wallet is now entered in the account settings instead of the miner’s pool settings. I remembered JD mentioning a change to the U.S. server, but I didn’t know the connection method had changed too. Without my wallet saved in the new account and the updated worker format, my miners couldn’t connect.
This is a serious communication problem. Changes to the server addresses and connection setup need to be announced by email or on the pool site. I was left offline and had to work out the changes myself.
I also had around 180,000 Bolts, and they’re now gone. Please explain why they were wiped and whether they can be restored.
Please do a better job notifying pool users before making changes that affect their miners and account balances.
Handed to the team · I can't see or restore pool accounts or Bolts balances. Also note: heliumdeploy.

Note to the team: I've passed Dean's Bolts question to the team. I can't see or restore pool accounts or Bolts balances myself, so it's flagged as a balance issue. The team picks it up tomorrow at 10am ET. Hi Dean, I'm glad both miners are mining again. I'm sorry you had to work out the new setup …
